title: In my opinion: agreeing, disagreeing and giving reasons
intro: So far you have described, compared and asked. Now you learn to say what you think – and why. You give your opinion with به نظر من and فکر می‌کنم که, agree and disagree without offending anyone, and back up your view with چون, زیرا and برای اینکه. The test case is an argument every Iranian family has had: is life better in the city or in the village?
goals: give your opinion with به نظر من and فکر می‌کنم که
ask other people what they think
agree, partly agree and disagree – politely
give reasons with چون، زیرا and برای اینکه
argue for and against city and village life

sections.title: Three tools for an argument
sections.md:
Every opinion in Persian is built from three small tools.

1. **Saying what you think.** [[به نظر من|be nazar-e man|in my opinion]] literally means *to my view*. Just as common is [[فکر می‌کنم که…|fekr mi-konam ke…|I think that…]] – and in speech the [[که|ke]] is usually dropped.
2. **Agreeing and disagreeing.** [[موافق|movāfegh|agreeing]] and [[مخالف|mokhālef|opposed]] are adjectives, so they take the to-be endings you learned in A1: [[موافقم|movāfegh-am|I agree]], [[مخالفم|mokhālef-am|I disagree]].
3. **Giving a reason.** [[چون|chon|because]] for every day, [[زیرا|zirā|because]] for writing, and [[برای اینکه|barā-ye inke|because]] when you answer a [[چرا؟|cherā?|why?]].

One more thing matters as much as the grammar: tone. Iranians argue with gusto, but a flat *you're wrong* sounds rude. Listen to how Mina says [[ببخشید، ولی…|bebakhshid, vali…|sorry, but…]] before she disagrees, and how Reza starts with [[حق با توست|hagh bā to-st|you're right]] before his *but*.

items.note: in speech usually به نظرم be nazar-am
to think about something: فکر کردن به
موافقم = I agree; موافق بودن با = to agree with
مخالفم = I disagree, I'm against it
درست است، اما… = that's true, but…
the everyday word; it can start a sentence
written style; never at the start of a sentence
also ده deh; in speech often دهات dehāt, 'the villages, the countryside'

sections.title: In my opinion: به نظر من and فکر می‌کنم که
sections.md:
[[نظر|nazar]] means *view, opinion*, so [[به نظر من|be nazar-e man]] is *to my view*. Swap the pronoun to talk about anyone: [[به نظر او|be nazar-e u|in his / her opinion]], [[به نظر شما|be nazar-e shomā|in your opinion]]. In speech the possessive endings are more common: [[به نظرم|be nazar-am]], [[به نظرت|be nazar-at]], [[به نظرش|be nazar-ash]].

[[فکر کردن|fekr kardan|to think]] is an ordinary compound verb, and what you think follows in a clause with [[که|ke|that]]: [[فکر می‌کنم که دیر است|fekr mi-konam ke dir ast|I think (that) it's late]]. As in English, *that* is often left out.

**I don't think…** – when you doubt something, the verb after [[فکر نمی‌کنم|fekr nemi-konam]] usually goes into the subjunctive you learned in lesson 4: [[فکر نمی‌کنم بیاید|fekr nemi-konam biyāyad|I don't think he'll come]]. The same happens after [[شاید|shāyad|maybe]].

sections.title: I agree, I disagree: موافقم، مخالفم
sections.md:
[[موافق|movāfegh]] and [[مخالف|mokhālef]] are adjectives, so you add the short to-be endings: [[موافقم|movāfegh-am|I agree]], [[موافقی؟|movāfegh-i?|do you agree?]], [[موافق است|movāfegh ast|he / she agrees]], [[موافقیم|movāfegh-im|we agree]], [[موافقید|movāfegh-id|you agree]], [[موافق‌اند|movāfegh-and|they agree]]. The person or idea you agree with takes [[با|bā|with]]: [[با شما موافقم|bā shomā movāfegh-am|I agree with you]].

[[مخالفم|mokhālef-am]] is strong – *I'm against it*. Most people soften it to [[موافق نیستم|movāfegh nistam|I don't agree]], or, more gently still, agree with part of what was said and then add [[اما|ammā]] or [[ولی|vali]]. The scale below runs from full agreement to a flat no:

sections.title: Because: چون، زیرا، برای اینکه
sections.md:
Persian has three common words for *because*, and they differ in style more than in meaning.

- [[چون|chon]] is the everyday one. It can come in the middle or at the very start: [[چون خسته بودم، زود خوابیدم.|chon khaste budam, zud khābidam.|Because I was tired, I went to bed early.]]
- [[زیرا|zirā]] belongs to writing, the news and speeches. It only joins two halves of a sentence – it never opens one.
- [[برای اینکه|barā-ye inke]] (literally *for this that*) is the natural answer to [[چرا؟|cherā?|why?]]. In Tehrani speech it is [[واسه اینکه|vāse inke]].

Before a **noun**, use [[به خاطر|be khāter-e|because of]]: [[به خاطر ترافیک|be khāter-e terāfik|because of the traffic]]. And to give the result instead of the reason, use [[برای همین|barā-ye hamin|that's why]] or [[به همین دلیل|be hamin dalil|for this reason]].

examples.faV: مادَربُزُرگَم دَر روستا زِندِگی می‌کُنَد، بَرایِ هَمین هَر سال به آن‌جا می‌رَویم.

sections.title: City or village? Tom's essay
sections.intro: Mr Karimi asked his class to write an انشا – a school essay – on an old question. Here is Tom's. Notice how he gives both sides with از یک طرف … از طرف دیگر (on the one hand … on the other) before his own opinion.

sentences.fa: زندگی در شهر بهتر است یا زندگی در روستا؟
sentences.r: zendegi dar shahr behtar ast yā zendegi dar rustā?
sentences.en: Is life better in the city or in the village?
sentences.faV: زِندِگی دَر شَهر بِهتَر اَست یا زِندِگی دَر روستا؟

sentences.fa: بسیاری از جوان‌های ایرانی به شهرهای بزرگ می‌روند، زیرا در شهر کار و دانشگاه هست.
sentences.r: besyāri az javān-hā-ye Irāni be shahr-hā-ye bozorg mi-ravand, zirā dar shahr kār o dāneshgāh hast.
sentences.en: Many young Iranians move to the big cities, because that is where the jobs and universities are.
sentences.faV: بِسیاری اَز جَوان‌هایِ ایرانی به شَهرهایِ بُزُرگ می‌رَوَند، زیرا دَر شَهر کار و دانِشگاه هَست.

sentences.fa: از یک طرف، شهر امکانات بیشتری دارد: بیمارستان، مترو، سینما و کتاب‌فروشی.
sentences.r: az yek taraf, shahr emkānāt-e bishtar-i dārad: bimārestān, metro, sinamā o ketāb-forushi.
sentences.en: On the one hand, the city has more facilities: hospitals, the metro, cinemas and bookshops.
sentences.faV: اَز یِک طَرَف، شَهر اِمکاناتِ بیشتَری دارَد: بیمارِستان، مِترو، سینَما و کِتاب‌فُروشی.

sentences.fa: از طرف دیگر، زندگی در شهر گران و شلوغ است.
sentences.r: az taraf-e digar, zendegi dar shahr gerān o sholugh ast.
sentences.en: On the other hand, city life is expensive and crowded.
sentences.faV: اَز طَرَفِ دیگَر، زِندِگی دَر شَهر گِران و شُلوغ اَست.

sentences.fa: در تهران هوا آلوده است و مردم ساعت‌ها در ترافیک می‌مانند.
sentences.r: dar Tehrān havā ālude ast o mardom sā'at-hā dar terāfik mi-mānand.
sentences.en: In Tehran the air is polluted and people sit in traffic for hours.
sentences.faV: دَر تِهران هَوا آلوده اَست و مَردُم ساعَت‌ها دَر تِرافیک می‌مانَند.

sentences.fa: در روستا زندگی آرام‌تر است و مردم همدیگر را می‌شناسند.
sentences.r: dar rustā zendegi ārām-tar ast o mardom hamdigar rā mi-shenāsand.
sentences.en: In a village life is calmer, and people know each other.
sentences.faV: دَر روستا زِندِگی آرام‌تَر اَست و مَردُم هَمدیگَر را می‌شِناسَند.

sentences.fa: اما به نظر من روستا یک مشکل بزرگ دارد: کار کم است.
sentences.r: ammā be nazar-e man rustā yek moshkel-e bozorg dārad: kār kam ast.
sentences.en: But in my opinion the village has one big problem: there isn't much work.
sentences.faV: اَمّا به نَظَرِ مَن روستا یِک مُشکِلِ بُزُرگ دارَد: کار کَم اَست.

sentences.fa: دوستم مینا فکر می‌کند که با اینترنت در روستا هم می‌تواند کار کند.
sentences.r: dust-am Minā fekr mi-konad ke bā internet dar rustā ham mi-tavānad kār konad.
sentences.en: My friend Mina thinks that with the internet she can work in a village too.
sentences.faV: دوستَم مینا فِکر می‌کُنَد که با اینتِرنِت دَر روستا هَم می‌تَوانَد کار کُنَد.

sentences.fa: من فقط تا حدی با او موافقم، چون اینترنت روستاها هنوز کند است.
sentences.r: man faghat tā hadd-i bā u movāfegh-am, chon internet-e rustā-hā hanuz kond ast.
sentences.en: I only partly agree with her, because the internet in villages is still slow.
sentences.note: کند here is kond, 'slow' – the same letters as konad, 'does'
sentences.faV: مَن فَقَط تا حَدّی با او مُوافِقَم، چون اینتِرنِتِ روستاها هَنوز کُند اَست.

sentences.fa: پس به نظر من بهترین راه این است که در شهر کار کنیم و آخر هفته‌ها به روستا برویم.
sentences.r: pas be nazar-e man behtarin rāh in ast ke dar shahr kār konim o ākhar-e hafte-hā be rustā beravim.
sentences.en: So in my opinion the best way is to work in the city and go to the village at weekends.
sentences.faV: پَس به نَظَرِ مَن بِهتَرین راه این اَست که دَر شَهر کار کُنیم و آخَرِ هَفته‌ها به روستا بِرَویم.

sections.title: From the village to the city – and back for Nowruz
sections.md:
Two generations ago most Iranians lived in villages: in the census of 1956 fewer than a third of the population was urban. Today about three Iranians in four live in towns and cities, and Tehran alone has more than eight million people. Yet almost every city family still has a village in its story – the [[ده|deh|village]] of a grandfather – and at Nowruz the roads out of Tehran fill with people going back to it.

Some villages have become sights in their own right: [[ماسوله|Māsule]] in the green hills of Gilan, built so steeply that the roof of one house is the yard of the house above, or red-earth [[ابیانه|Abyāne]] near Kashan, where older women still wear long white headscarves printed with flowers.

The argument itself is a school classic. Generations of Iranian children have had to write an [[انشا|enshā|essay]] on the question [[علم بهتر است یا ثروت؟|elm behtar ast yā servat?|Is knowledge better, or wealth?]] – so many that the title has become shorthand for a tired school topic. *City or village?* is its close cousin, and every Iranian has an opinion on it.

sections.title: Tips
items: **Disagree softly.** A flat **مخالفم** can sound rude to an older person or a guest. Start with **درست است، اما…** (that's true, but…), **ببخشید، ولی…** (sorry, but…) or **شاید حق با شما باشد، ولی…** – and then say what you like.
**زیرا never starts a sentence.** To put the reason first, use **چون**: *chon khaste budam, zud khābidam* – because I was tired, I went to bed early.
**موافقم is one word with two parts**: movāfegh + -am (I am). Change the ending for other people: **موافقی؟** (do you agree?), **موافق‌اند** (they agree).
**کند** can be *konad* (does) or *kond* (slow) – the same letters. The sentence tells you which.
In speech **به نظر من** becomes **به نظرم**, **برای اینکه** becomes **واسه اینکه**, and **فکر می‌کنم** often becomes **فکر کنم** – a casual *I guess*.

items.explain: The person you agree with takes با: bā shomā movāfegh-am.

items.q: Which 'because' belongs in a newspaper article?
items.explain: zirā is formal and written; vāse inke is spoken Tehrani, and barā-ye hamin means 'that's why'.

items.q: You want to disagree politely with an older colleague. The best way to start:
items.explain: Agree with part of what was said, then add your 'but'.
fekr kardan = to think; che kār mi-konid? = what are you doing?
After 'I don't think' Persian normally uses the subjunctive: biyāyad.

items.q: Which word can NOT start a sentence?
items.explain: zirā only joins the two halves of a sentence; start with chon instead.

items.en: I'm not coming today, because I'm ill.
I don't think he'll come today.
Because of the traffic, I arrived late.

items.fa: به نظر من زندگی در روستا آرام‌تر است.
items.r: be nazar-e man zendegi dar rustā ārām-tar ast.
items.en: In my opinion life in a village is calmer.
items.faV: به نَظَرِ مَن زِندِگی دَر روستا آرام‌تَر اَست.

items.fa: چون ماشین نداشتم، با مترو آمدم.
items.r: chon māshin na-dāshtam, bā metro āmadam.
items.en: Because I didn't have a car, I came by metro.
items.faV: چون ماشین نَداشتَم، با مِترو آمَدَم.

items.en: I agree up to a point.
options: I agree up to a point.

items.r: be nazar-e man zendegi dar shahr rāhat-tar ast.
items.faV: به نَظَرِ مَن زِندِگی دَر شَهر راحَت‌تَر اَست.
